summary.text: Cynthia (Cinde) Wirth is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 6th Congressional District. A Columbus, Indiana native, she has worked as a high school science teacher, small business owner, researcher, and federal legislative fellow. She was the Democratic nominee in 2024 and says she is running on health care, education and affordability.

paragraphs.text: Wirth was born and raised in Columbus, Indiana, and graduated from Columbus North High School. She describes herself as a first-generation college graduate.

She earned a B.A. in biology and Spanish from the University of Evansville in 1992, an M.A. in anthropology/archaeology/underwater cultural resource management from Indiana University Bloomington in 2009, and a Ph.D. from Ball State University in 2025.

Wirth worked as a high school biology and environmental science teacher, a research consultant, and a facilitator of biology and environmental science with CSA New Tech, and has been a small business owner. Her campaign website says she taught at Columbus Signature Academy for more than 10 years and has owned a community business for more than 20 years.

She was selected as an Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellow with the U.S. Department of Energy as a legislative fellow. Her campaign website says she served as a science and education expert for the U.S. House of Representatives in 2018 and 2019 and that one of the federal bills she wrote there became law in 2020.
Wirth has served as an Educational Ambassador for Friends of Miyoshi, Japan, and her Ballotpedia profile lists professional affiliations including archaeology societies and Sunrise Rotary.

She ran for the seat in 2024 as the Democratic nominee and lost the general election to Jefferson Shreve, 31.7% to 63.9%. According to her campaign website, she also had a congressional campaign in 2022.
According to her campaign materials, she and her husband, Trent, have lived in downtown Columbus for 30 years and have two grown children.
